concept: Divider is the seam between two regions of one unit, cut into the plastic the way a panel gap is: a shade edge over a lit edge, one pixel each. It parts what sits above from what sits below and says nothing itself, except an optional lowercase word printed on the line.

default_to_avoid.pattern: divider as a single grey 1px rule across the full width, with an 'OR' pill centred on it
default_to_avoid.why_not: A hard rule cuts the unit in two with a drawn line instead of a cut seam, and a centred pill floats mid-surface instead of sitting on the inset line.

default_to_avoid.pattern: divider with a dark or accent-coloured rule between regions of one unit
default_to_avoid.why_not: FORM.md forbids a hard dark rule inside a unit, and orange belongs to the unit's one primary control only.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams and Hans Gugelot, 1956): the panel gap between the lid, the speaker and the controls is the only separator
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band names printed on the case along a scale line
system/FORM.md separator class: a seam, 1px, no depth, gaps first

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The seam is cut into the body with the inverse light: the divider tone on its top-left edge and the material's lit tone on the bottom-right edge, so it reads as a gap and not as a drawn rule.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: A label is printed on the seam itself, a short inset from its start, and the seam carries on after it, so the word is never set mid-surface.

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material, with no shadow and no emboss
derivation.form: The label is flat printing in secondary ink with no shadow, and only the seam either side of it is cut.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The seam takes a fixed two pixels, and a label never changes its height, so the regions it parts do not move.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The seam and its label are ink and plastic tones. A divider is never orange.

options.name: one hairline in the divider tone
cut seam, shade edge over lit edge

variants.reason: B follows the light model (a recess has shade on top-left and a lit edge bottom-right), so it reads as a panel gap; A is the generic one-pixel grey rule, and C copies the dotted rail Stepper and Breadcrumb already own and its dashes read as a dashed border.

root.why: The seam: a shade edge over a lit edge, two pixels in all, running the width of its column or the height of its row.

label.why: The printed word sits on the seam in the label size and secondary ink, with the seam running on both sides of it.

data-orientation=vertical.why: A vertical seam stretches to the height of its row and takes the two edges on its inline sides, so it parts side-by-side regions at the same two pixels.

data-labelled.why: With a label the seam splits into a short lead and a long run either side of the word, so the word sits on the inset line.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the lit edge is dropped and the shade edge draws in the system grey, so the seam stays one visible line.
